question: Why does Greenland look so huge on the usual world map?
answer: Greenland looks huge on the usual world map because Mercator's projection stretches land more the farther it sits from the equator, both wider and taller at once. Up by the Arctic Circle, Greenland is blown up many times over, drawn about ×14 its real size. Slid down to the equator, its real area of 2.16 million km² shows.
move: On a Mercator map, the nearer a pole, the bigger it lies.
